question.text: Under Section 11C of the SEBI Act, SEBI can direct investigation when it has reasonable grounds to believe that:

answer.text: An intermediary has failed to pay its annual fees to SEBI
Transactions in securities are being dealt with in a manner detrimental to investors or the securities market
A company has delayed its annual general meeting by more than 30 days
Stock exchange turnover has declined below a prescribed threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 11C of the SEBI Act empowers SEBI to direct investigation when it has reasonable ground to believe that securities transactions are being dealt with in a manner detrimental to investors or the securities market, or that an intermediary or associated person has violated SEBI Act provisions, rules, regulations or directions. The Trap: Annual fee non-payment, AGM delays and turnover thresholds are not the statutory triggers in Section 11C - they sit under other administrative or company-law provisions. Section 11C is specifically about investigation of market-detrimental conduct or regulatory violations. Note: Page 29 of the workbook supports the Section 11C grounds quoted above.
